issues.legal_issue: A preliminary acquisition notification for land intended for a company is not invalid merely because it does not expressly state that the acquisition is for a public purpose.
material_facts: The preliminary notification said the land was likely to be needed for a company’s factory buildings and related purposes, but did not expressly describe the acquisition as being for a public purpose.
The statutory inquiry into the purpose of the company acquisition had not been completed when the challenge was brought.
issues.conclusion: An express statement of public purpose in the preliminary notification was not essential; the requirement was met if the inquiry established, and the appropriate government was satisfied, that the acquisition purpose was one contemplated for company acquisitions under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4 and 5A, the preliminary notification initiates investigation, while section 6 provides for a firm declaration. For an acquisition for a company, sections 39–41 and section 40 require the appropriate government’s consent and an agreement, and the government must be satisfied that the acquisition serves a purpose specified in section 40. Such purposes, including work useful to the public and housing or amenities for employees, fall within the generic meaning of public purpose in section 3. The Court relied on State of Bombay v. Bhanji Munji for the principle that an express statement of public purpose is not invariably necessary if that purpose can be gathered from the law and proceedings.

rule.if: company_land_acquisition and preliminary_notice_only and notice_omitted_public_purpose and purpose_inquiry_pending

predicates.company_land_acquisition: The government initiated compulsory acquisition proceedings for land intended for a company.
predicates.preliminary_notice_only: Only a preliminary notice had been issued, and no final declaration had yet been made.
predicates.notice_omitted_public_purpose: The preliminary notice identified the intended company use but did not expressly call it a public purpose.
predicates.purpose_inquiry_pending: The inquiry into whether the company’s intended use qualified for acquisition had not been completed.

issues.definition: When a company land acquisition is still at the preliminary-notice stage, omission of an express public-purpose statement does not by itself make the notice invalid while the purpose inquiry remains pending.

issues.legal_issue: A constitutional challenge to company land-acquisition proceedings is premature while the preliminary inquiry into the acquisition’s purpose remains unresolved.
material_facts: Only a preliminary notification had been issued when the petition was filed.
The inquiry into the company’s proposed acquisition purpose was still in progress, and the government had not yet made its decision on that purpose or issued a final declaration.
issues.conclusion: The petition was premature because the purpose of the acquisition had not yet been investigated and determined through the statutory process.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5A and 6 provide for an inquiry into objections followed by the government’s declaration, and sections 39 and 40 require satisfaction on the permitted purpose before the acquisition machinery can proceed for a company. A preliminary notification begins investigation; it is not the final determination that the land is needed for the stated purpose.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_acquisition: An interested person brought a constitutional proceeding challenging compulsory acquisition.
predicates.preliminary_notice_only: The proceeding was brought after a preliminary notice but before a final acquisition declaration.
predicates.purpose_inquiry_unresolved: The statutory inquiry and government determination of the acquisition purpose were still pending.

issues.definition: A constitutional challenge to an acquisition is premature when it is brought after only a preliminary notice and before the purpose inquiry has been resolved.

issues.legal_issue: The existing land-acquisition law was not invalid under the constitutional guarantee governing compulsory acquisition on the ground that acquisition for a company might not serve a public purpose.
material_facts: The challenged proceedings were initiated under a law that existed before the Constitution came into force.
The Court held that the constitutional exception concerning a specified class of laws did not apply to that law.
For company acquisitions, the statutory machinery could not proceed without the government’s satisfaction as to a purpose specified for such acquisitions.
issues.conclusion: The challenge under the constitutional guarantee governing compulsory acquisition failed because the existing law was saved by the applicable constitutional exception.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2) required compulsory acquisition to be for a public purpose and by authority of law, but Article 31(5)(a) preserved existing laws other than laws within Article 31(6). The Court relied on Lilavati Bai v. State of Bombay. It also noted that the company-acquisition requirements in Part VII, including section 40, restrict the acquisition purposes that can activate the statutory machinery; it did not decide whether every acquisition for a company is necessarily for a public purpose.

predicates.constitutional_compulsory_acquisition_ch: A person challenged compulsory acquisition as inconsistent with the constitutional protection governing such acquisition.
predicates.preexisting_acquisition_law: The acquisition was carried out under a law that existed before the Constitution came into force.
predicates.special_exception_inapplicable: The law did not fall within the special class excluded from the constitutional saving for existing laws.

issues.definition: A challenge under the constitutional protection governing compulsory acquisition fails when the acquisition rests on a pre-existing law that is covered by the saving for existing laws.

issues.legal_issue: Compulsory acquisition proceedings under the land-acquisition law did not violate the constitutional freedom invoked to protect property.
material_facts: The petitioner, who claimed an ownership interest in the land, challenged compulsory acquisition proceedings under the land-acquisition law.
The challenge relied on the constitutional freedom invoked to protect property.
issues.conclusion: The challenge under that constitutional freedom failed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court rejected the challenge in view of State of Bombay v. Bhanji Munji and Lilavati Bai v. State of Bombay.

predicates.constitutional_property_freedom_challeng: A person challenged government action as violating the constitutional freedom that the person invoked to protect property.
predicates.compulsory_land_acquisition: The challenged government action was compulsory acquisition of land under the land-acquisition process.

issues.definition: A challenge invoking the constitutional property freedom fails where the challenged action is compulsory land acquisition.
